answer: Mutual insurance pools stop fake identities by tying ten strangers to a bond. The pool atlas lists members and stakes, so copies cannot hide behind new names. A comet audit can freeze any pool, so fake claims cannot dodge reviews. If one member is proved fake, the pool's 1,000-credit bond is slashed, so honest members vet newcomers. A relic record of work must match claim, or payment is held. The kth fake needs a new 100-credit stake, so 1,000 fakes lock 100,000 credits, while an honest agent pays 100 once. Pool farming fails because rented strangers lack matching records.
